windward-lee.cap: Blick von achtern. Das Boot krängt nach Lee.

texts.rationale: The arrows show airflow, not a compass course.
The side of the boat toward the incoming wind; confirmed by the arrows entering from the left.
This explains the wind-facing side, not meteorological weather.
Weather side is the nautical synonym for windward; a literal Wetterseite is unnecessary for this learner diagram.
The boat side facing away from the wind, shown on the right.
Uses the defining direction instead of promising that this side is always sheltered.
Here limits the boom-side statement to the illustrated sailing position, not every manoeuvre or backwinded configuration.
Boat-relative wording avoids the ambiguous shore-relative compound Leeküste; this is the shore downwind of the boat.
The illustrated downwind coast is the grounding hazard; the wind drives the boat toward land.
Boat-relative wording preserves weather shore: the coast from which wind comes, not a weather forecast or the exposed side of an island.
Ablandiger Wind means airflow from land toward water. Drops the unconditional shelter claim; offshore wind alone does not guarantee protection.

windward-lee.capRationale: The view looks forward from behind the stern, so von achtern is correct. Krängen is the nautical verb for heeling. The drawing shows a heel to the right, away from wind entering from the left, hence nach Lee.
windward-lee.noteRationale: The source note is empty, so there is no note text to translate.

mooring-lines.cap: Längsseits am Steg, von oben gesehen. Der Bug zeigt nach rechts.

texts.rationale: Plural German Fender names the hull-protection cushions; not a road-vehicle wing.
The German sail-training glossary defines this as a line led athwartships to shore; the red line runs square across from amidships.
Its transverse lead checks the boat moving away from the pontoon; this is not a spring.
The after-end mooring line, led aft of the stern in this plan view.
The stern is at the left; its line leads farther aft to the lower-left shore cleat.
A mooring line from the bow, not Palstek, which would translate the knot bowline.
The bow is at the right and this line leads farther forward to the lower-right shore cleat.
Named by its forward onboard origin, although the line leads aft; the SVG shows that exact geometry.
The forward green line runs aft to the shore cleat left of its onboard attachment.
A line leading aft opposes forward movement of the boat; the restraint must not be reversed.
Named by its aft onboard origin, although the line leads forward.
The aft green line runs forward to the shore cleat right of its onboard attachment.
A line leading forward opposes aft movement; matches the source diagram and the existing course card.

mooring-lines.capRationale: The boat is shown in plan parallel to the pontoon, hence längsseits am Steg; the pointed bow is at the right. Längsseits and Bug are sailing terminology confirmed by the specialist references.
mooring-lines.noteRationale: The source note is empty, so there is no note text to translate.
